question: What is the modern digital replacement for the traditional paper medical chart?
explanation: Think of the Electronic Health Record (EHR) as the digital upgrade to our old paper charts. It keeps all patient info neat, organized, and easy to access in one place! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does moving from paper charts to EHR systems help keep patients safer with their medications?

options.A: By ensuring doctors prescribe only generic medications
options.B: By eliminating errors linked to poor handwriting
options.C: By removing the need for nurses to calculate drug doses
options.D: By automatically administering drugs via the system

explanation: We've all struggled to read messy doctor's handwriting! Typing orders into an EHR takes away that guesswork, keeping our patients safe from medication mix-ups. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which clinical environment is best suited for an ambulatory EHR system?
explanation: Ambulatory EHRs are made for places where patients come and go quickly, like outpatient or community clinics for routine checkups. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: What makes acute care EHR systems different from ambulatory ones?

options.A: Ambulatory platforms are restricted to emergency room triage
options.B: Ambulatory systems require specialized surgical scheduling modules
options.C: Acute care software only stores pharmacy billing data
options.D: Acute care systems track continuous inpatient monitoring and hourly vitals

explanation: In an inpatient ward, patients stay overnight, so the EHR needs to track round-the-clock care, like hourly vital signs and continuous nursing notes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which feature is a must-have in a pediatric EHR system?
explanation: Children aren't just small adults! Their drug doses depend heavily on their body weight, so having a calculator right in the EHR helps us prevent dangerous dosing errors. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why do mental health units use specialized psychiatric EHR software?

options.A: To maintain strict privacy controls for sensitive behavioral health notes
options.B: To monitor continuous intravenous fluid drips in the ward
options.C: To automatically calculate pediatric immunization schedules
options.D: To manage emergency surgical theater equipment inventories

explanation: Behavioral health notes are deeply personal. Specialized software gives them extra-tight security and privacy protection so only the right care team can view them. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of an enterprise EHR system in a big hospital?

options.A: Operating strictly within outpatient community health posts
options.B: Connecting all clinical and administrative departments into one database
options.C: Managing financial payroll exclusively for medical doctors
options.D: Replacing the need for individual nursing documentation notes

explanation: An enterprise EHR acts like the central nervous system of a large hospital, linking every department together so everyone shares the same patient information smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: A nurse logs a new drug administration into an enterprise EHR. What happens immediately across the hospital?

options.A: Laboratory results are immediately deleted to save storage
options.B: The hospital internet connection shuts down for security
options.C: Pharmacy inventory and patient billing update instantly
options.D: The patient's physical paper folder is automatically printed

explanation: That's the beauty of an integrated hospital system! One click at the bedside updates pharmacy stocks and patient bills automatically behind the scenes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: Who is primarily in charge of managing a Personal Health Record (PHR)?
explanation: Unlike hospital records, a Personal Health Record belongs to the patient. They manage, update, and carry it wherever they go! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of a patient portal linked to a hospital EHR?

options.A: Replacing all face-to-face nursing consultations in the clinic
options.B: Serving as the sole database for emergency surgical operations
options.C: Allowing patients to view lab results and communicate with providers
options.D: Enabling nurses to input hourly vital signs remotely from home

explanation: Patient portals empower individuals by letting them check their own test results and chat securely with their healthcare team right from their phones. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h5)

question: Where is patient data kept when a hospital uses an on-premise EHR system?

options.A: On physical servers housed inside the hospital building
options.B: Inside external government cloud storage hubs only
options.C: On remote external servers accessed via the internet
options.D: Exclusively on individual nurses' mobile smartphones

explanation: An 'on-premise' system means the physical computer servers live right there inside the hospital building, managed by their own IT staff. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is absolutely essential for running a cloud-based EHR smoothly?

options.B: Manual daily backups onto physical cassette tapes
options.C: A massive team of on-site computer hardware engineers
options.D: Large rooms dedicated solely to physical server racks

explanation: Since cloud systems store data on remote servers over the web, you need a steady internet connection to pull up and update patient records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: What does EHR interoperability help different healthcare computer systems do?

options.A: Exchange and read patient data accurately
options.B: Share financial profits between competing hospitals
options.C: Print paper charts faster during morning ward rounds
options.D: Automatically order medications without a doctor's review

explanation: Interoperability is just a fancy word for teamwork among software. It means different computer systems can talk to and understand each other. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why do we use standardized medical codes like ICD-10 in electronic health records?

options.A: They prevent patients from accessing their personal health portals
options.B: They automatically calculate the hospital electricity bill
options.C: They ensure a diagnosis means the exact same thing across different facilities
options.D: They eliminate the need for nurses to record vital signs

explanation: Standard codes make sure that a diagnosis written in Lagos means the exact same thing in Abuja or anywhere else, preventing any clinical confusion. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which technology helps nurses stop medication errors right at the patient's bedside?
explanation: Scanning patient wristbands and drug barcodes right before giving meds is a fantastic safety net that stops errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is a major safety hazard caused by poorly designed EHR warning systems on the ward?

options.A: Automatic deletion of vital sign records after every shift change
options.B: Alert fatigue causing nurses to overlook important safety warnings
options.C: Increased face-to-face communication between doctors and patients
options.D: Sudden physical hardware failure of all bedside computers

explanation: When a computer pops up too many unnecessary warnings, nurses get 'alert fatigue' and might accidentally swipe past a real, serious danger. Balance is key! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h8)
